senses.definition: a thing or group of things in a disagreeable, disorganised, or dirty state; hence a bad situation
examples: No, look, I know that the place looks like a bit of a mess but it's actually a very delicate ecosystem. Everything is connected. It's like the rainforest. You change one thing, even the tiniest bit, and the whooole rainforest dies. You don't want the rainforest to die, do ya?
He made a mess of it.
My bedroom is such a mess; I need to tidy up.

senses.definition: (colloquial) a large quantity or number
examples: My boss dumped a whole mess of projects on my desk today.
She brought back a mess of fish to fix for supper.

quotes.text: Messerschmidts! A whole mess of Messerschmidts!

senses.definition: (euphemistic) excrement.
examples: There was dog mess all along the street.
Did you hear that? It scared the mess out of me.

senses.definition: (figuratively) a person in a state of (especially emotional) turmoil or disarray; an emotional wreck
examples: Between the pain and the depression, I'm a mess.
He's been a mess and a half ever since you excommunicated him.

quotes.text: I'm a mess in a dress, can't show up on time even if it would save my life. According to you.

senses.definition: (transitive, often with "up") To make untidy or dirty.

quotes.text: It seems like all you do is cry, eat, and mess your diapers!

senses.definition: (transitive, often with "up") To throw into disorder or to ruin.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To interfere.
examples: This doesn't concern you. Don't mess.

quotes.text: Eton is renowned for its "messes," and "strawberry mess" is Empress of them all, with raspberry mess as a very good second. It does not at all convey the joys of a "mess" to say that it consists of iced fruit and cream, and somewhat resembles a "fool." It is a thing apart, and should be approached with bated breath and unimpaired capacity.

"I'll stand you both strawberry mess." It was perfectly impossible for David not to feel elated at sitting down to strawberry-mess with two members of the eleven, in the full light of day, and in sight of the school generally […]

quotes.text: Eton mess, for example, which is another name for strawberry fool, links the name of a famous public school with disorder or the army slang for a meal, [...] One friend remembered a banana mess of mashed banana with two scoops of ice cream and loads of cream, and thought the strawberry version something that might be served at the 4th June College picnic, [...]
Similar desserts [to Eton Mess] include Lancing Mess (made with bananas), served at Lancing College in Sussex, and Clare College Mush[…]
